text: The hand comes down. Borro takes it on his shield, and Jaeha, with his palms on Borro's back, pulls the whole blow through Borro and into himself.
He doesn't pass it on. He holds it. His skin glows white-gold, cracks of light running up his arms, and his bones creak.
Store: one strike, three hundred and forty percent. It's so heavy that his thirty seconds of hold drop to ten.
Ten seconds. Then his bones go.
The blow has simply vanished, and her hand lifts away. He's holding it, Geum says. Jaeha has ten seconds, and he needs to reach her head.
Every link he has lights up at once: amber, green, blue, lilac. And from Moon Ahin's baton, her own cyan threads run to the twelve husks at the forearm.
Summons go first. Nib runs up her forearm, cutting a path through the barnacles.
Lyra shoots out the bars of her lantern, breaking the glare.
Moon Ahin conducts, and her twelve husks leap onto the leviathan's flank and lock together into a stair.
And Geum grabs Jaeha by the collar with her steel hand. Go, kid.
She throws him like a comet, straight at the white stair on the leviathan's flank.
Seven seconds left.
From the light tower, Pim calls every step he takes. Left foot. The rusty plate. Jump.
He runs up the stair of husks, and they crack under his feet one by one.
Her other hand knocks the lower steps into the sea, but he's already on her back.
Three seconds. He lands on top of her head, beside the long violet crack in her brow.
From up here, he can see the whole harbour. And far out on the black sea, three fishing boats that never made it home, lost in a violet haze.
Pim's antennae turn toward her, and his eyes fill up. He can hear her now, under the Hush.
A small voice, deep inside the crack. Take them home.
Out on the water, an old fisherman peers into the haze. He can't see the lighthouse, and has no idea which way the harbour is.
Two seconds. I'm not him, Jaeha tells her. I didn't stop. Let's take them home.
All the light in his body pours down his arm into his right fist, until it blazes like a small sun.
And for the first time in more than three hundred raids, Jaeha strikes with his own hand. Release.
The crack shatters, and the Hush pours out of her like smoke.
Her eye clears, from dull violet to a gentle sea-grey.
And her lantern burns white again. For one moment she is what she used to be: a lighthouse.
Her beam sweeps the sea, and the three lost boats turn toward it and come safely in.
On the pier, people who crept back to the water watch them come home, with their hands over their mouths.
Pim is crying. He hears her say her real name. Oriel.
Boss defeated: the Deep Lantern. Jaeha's first kill.
A new skill, Release. Route Alignment back up to seventy percent. And the sea gate is closing.
Oriel sinks slowly into the harbour and dissolves into light, and far out at sea, the gate closes.
And Jaeha falls thirty metres toward the black water, his right arm broken.
Lyra dives after him.
She catches him in the dark water and kicks for the light above.
Borro reaches down and hauls them both out, one in each hand.
That's twice this week he's made her swim. Put it on his bill.
Out over the water, her core still glows. The window offers harvest, and nothing else.
She wants to go home, Pim says. Once, there was a release button. Now there's only harvest.
And a Kanghan boat is racing toward the core.
If he leaves her here, they'll chain what's left of her.
So he presses harvest.
The core flies into his hand a second before their net reaches it. He'll find that button, he promises her. He'll take her home.
The light inside the coral pulses once, slowly, like an answer.
On the barge, Han Sora laughs out loud. The Director is going to hate this.
By nine-thirty, the harbour is calm, and the breakwater is full of people.
Yerin does what she can for his arm. It's broken in two places.
And Seoa, crying and furious, holds out a bowl. Dinner. Now.
The aunties feed everyone on the breakwater: summons, husks, rescuers, fishermen and the whole neighbourhood.
Pim is declared a hero and buried in fish cakes. He's an adult signal officer. But yes, please.
Over six million people are watching.
And all along the harbour, the people of Busan raise their fists and chant for the Trap Rats.
Moon Ahin sits with her husks, all twenty-eight of them, cracked but home. He gave them back to her, in the middle of all that. They were always hers, he says.
Geum sits down beside him with a bowl. One more set? Tomorrow.
Geum throws her head back and laughs. And a window closes the quest: capacity a hundred and eighteen percent, body rating F-plus.
In Seoul, Director Baek watches the stream from his office.
Hwang asks if they should act. No.
Let him get strong. Strong things are easier to keep.
His finger taps the violet core on his cane, once.
After midnight, everyone on the breakwater is asleep, except Pim.
Then his antennae snap upright, glowing.
Very far away, inside some gate, something small is tapping. Short, short, long.
Someone is calling from inside a gate. Small and scared. A scout's call sign, tapped on stone.
Nib's knives fall out of his hands and clatter on the stone.
Nib whispers a name. Kett.
His apprentice, missing since the Ninth Wall fell. Someone out there is still calling.
